top.title: Forget Ganon, Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Most Overlooked Boss Finally Gets Its Due
top.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is iconic for plenty of reasons, but a big part of that is thanks to its villain. Ganondorf is one of gaming’s great bad guys, a reputation that has only been enhanced by appearances in later games like Wind Waker and Tears of the Kingdom . While Ocarina of Time ’s Switch 2 remake does the Demon King justice, it’s also a reminder that the Zelda series has another excellent, and far more underappreciated, foe: Twinrova.

top.title: Detroit Pistons Announce Concerning Duncan Robinson Injury Update
top.description: The Detroit Pistons have received some concerning injury news during Saturday night’s matchup against the Miami Heat, and it involves one of their most productive offensive players. According to the team’s official public relations account , Duncan Robinson is questionable to return due to left thigh soreness . Robinson exited the first half with 4:17 remaining and did not return to begin the second half. Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press initially noted Robinson’s absence after halftime, reporting that the veteran sharpshooter had not returned to the floor. Shortly afterward, the Pistons confirmed the injury designation, leaving his availability for the remainder of the game uncertain. Nov 12, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Detroit Pistons forward Duncan Robinson (55) celebrates with Pistons guard Ausar Thompson (9) and Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) after making a go-ahead three point field goal against the Washington Wizards during the second overtime at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Duncan Robinson Injury Adds to Pistons’ Concerns The potential loss of Robinson would be another frustrating development for a Detroit team already dealing with significant injuries. Starting center Jalen Duren remains sidelined with a right hamstring strain, while guard Isaiah Joe was also ruled out of Saturday’s game with a right hip contusion, according to the NBA’s official injury report . Robinson has been one of Detroit’s most valuable offensive contributors early in the 2026-27 season, providing much-needed perimeter shooting alongside Cade Cunningham. His impressive start has already created an interesting contract decision for the Pistons , who must decide whether to fully guarantee his salary later this season. The 32-year-old entered the season with plenty to prove and has responded by becoming a major piece of Detroit’s offense. His ability to stretch the floor has been especially important with Duren unavailable and head coach J.B. Bickerstaff adjusting his rotations. Detroit recently moved Daniss Jenkins into the starting lineup , giving the Pistons another offensive contributor alongside Cunningham and Robinson. If Robinson cannot return, Detroit will need additional production from its remaining perimeter players. For now, the Pistons have not announced that Robinson is officially out for the remainder of Saturday’s game. The team will continue evaluating his status, and additional information regarding the severity of his thigh soreness has not been released.

top.title: Fiji 'did Ireland a favour' before South Africa game
top.description: Fiji boss Jake White (left) believes Andy Farrell (right) and Ireland must improve before facing South Africa [Getty Images] Former South Africa head coach Jake White said his Fiji side "did Ireland a favour" in Saturday's Nations Championship contest before the Irish face the Springboks in Dublin next week. Fiji lost 43-15 to Ireland at Aviva Stadium having frustrated Andy Farrell's side during a closely contested first half. While Ireland scored 26 unanswered points in the second half, White - who led South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007 - said Andy Farrell's team cannot afford similarly sluggish spells against the back-to-back world champions. "We were playing a little bit like South Africa to be honest, I think that sums it up," said the 62-year-old. "We were letting Ireland have the ball and we were happy to defend against them and we were happy for them to try to outwork us." Asked to assess Ireland and South Africa's highly-anticipated meeting on Saturday (16:40 GMT), White added: "Well, I think we probably did Ireland a favour today. "Let me put it that way, because I think Ireland deep down know that if they play like that against South Africa, they're gonna be up against it." Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji White, who was appointed Fiji boss last month, was frustrated that his side opted to take a tap penalty instead of a scrum when the game was in the balance in the second half. "I know how South Africa operate and they would've taken that scrum there, they would have backed the fact that they wanted to get [Ireland] a yellow card," said White. "They would have taken another scrum and another scrum and another scrum, and they wouldn't have worried about the ref making a call about collapsing or early engaging. "The five-metre line-outs that we didn't take opportunities in, and the five-metre scrum and tap penalties, South Africa will turn those into points and I'm sure that Andy [Farrell] and the players will be aware of that. "They [Ireland] have been around a long time, and they know what's coming, and that's probably why he picked the team that he did because he wanted to make sure that they get a little bit more gun-ready for next weekend, because the easiest thing would have been to change the team and then they're probably one game shy of playing South Africa next week." White added: "If I'm coaching South Africa and Malcolm Marx is standing there [as captain], there's no way he is going to say, 'we'll take the tap'. There's no way that happens. "Malcolm Marx will say, 'let's take the scrum,' or 'we'll kick it out into the corner and we'll take the line-out'. And that's because they back themselves in those situations." When White's comments were put to Farrell, the Ireland boss said: "We were just saying in the changing rooms that we learned some good lessons and we'll use them in the right manner for next week." top.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 14: Christian Pulisic #10 of United States celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammates during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images In their first competitive match since their World Cup loss to Belgium, and their penultimate match under Mauricio Pochettino, the US soundly handled Haiti in Nations League play by a final score of 6-0. The match started out more slowly than the final score would indicate with the US tallying just once in the opening half, the goal coming on an Auston Trusty header off a Sebastian Berhalter free kick in the 10th minute. Diego Kochen had to make a big stop in the 15th minute to keep things level but the US would dominate possession and go into the half up 1-0. The US would come out flying in the second half with Julian Hall scoring his first goal in a competitive match for the USMNT, Christian Pulisic would score a brace, and Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun would add to the tally as well. A second Haiti opportunity would be called back due to a narrow offsides, saving Kochen some embarrassment after coming out of his goal but failing to clear, and the match would finish 6-0. It was an eventful match and included first time caps for goal scorer Julian Hall as well as Justin Hall, Adri Mehmeti, and Mathis Albert who would come in as second half substitutes. Thanks to the result, the US will go into the second leg of their Nations League quarter-final matchup needing simply to not loose by six goals in Mauricio Pochettino’s final match to move on to the semi-finals next March. top.title: St. Mary's water polo falls short to Rio Americano in CIF SJS final
top.description: It was simply one of those days. St. Mary's girls water polo had no shortage of opportunities . Shots glanced off the crossbar. Chances inside 2 meters disappeared before a shot could be taken. Even wide-open looks in front of the goal failed to find the net. Unfortunately for the Rams, it came at the worst possible time . In Saturday's CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division II championship game, No. 1 St. Mary's suffered its second straight loss in the section final , falling 8-4 to No. 2 Rio Americano, the Capital Valley Conference champion, at North Natomas Aquatic Complex on Nov. 14. "It felt like every time we had the perfect opportunity, we just missed the mark," Loyola Marymount commit Reyna Biedermann said. "Even when we made a cutoff and had a chance to go on offense, somehow they kept the ball. Things just didn't go our way." The TCAL champion entered averaging nearly 14 goals per game but managed just four, its second-lowest total of the season. Reyna, Denali Elliott, Gemma Lichter and Ella Fernandez were the Rams' goal scorers. "I get choked up just trying to describe this group," St. Mary's coach Vanessa Vincent said. "We've worked so hard for so long to get here. We didn't get to lift our first banner, but regardless of the outcome, I couldn't be more proud." Rio Americano, meanwhile, got two goals from Hannah Holladay and one apiece from six other players. "We believe that everybody's a participant on our team, and everybody practices hard," Rio Americano coach Rachel Ruano said. "It's nice that they can step into those big moments." 'Just didn't go in' The start was promising. Rio Americano took an early 1-0 lead on Alexa Kronbetter's goal, but St. Mary's responded. Reyna converted from 5 meters, and Emery Biedermann found Elliott on a step-out play. Then the scoring stopped. For St. Mary's, the drought stretched all the way to the 3:47 mark of the fourth quarter. "We could've made those adjustments earlier," Vincent said. "We eventually did, but the shots just weren't falling. Their goalie was reading us really well, and they pressured us hard. We were taking good shots. They just didn't go in." It began with 10 seconds left in the first quarter. Claire McGrath and Erin Ash had just put Rio Americano ahead 3-2 when Reyna sent a lob shot off the crossbar. The second quarter brought more of the same, only worse. Hannah Holladay scored from outside, while Reyna and Emery each missed a 5-meter attempt. St. Mary's then had a one-on-one shot from 2 meters blocked before another attempt during a 6-on-5 advantage was saved, sending the Rams into halftime down 4-2. "Everybody played great," Ruano said. "It was really fun seeing our bench come in and score a couple of goals." And the third quarter wasn't much different. Harper Bowers added another goal for Rio Americano, while St. Mary's went the first four minutes without even attempting a shot. When Reyna finally got a chance, her attempt hit the crossbar again. top.description: THE CHAMPS ARE HERE | Credit: Marquette University In August, I led off the Three Questions part of the Marquette volleyball season preview with “Who’s doing what around here, anyway?” as the first question. Pretty much everything was up for grabs in Tom Mendoza’s second season in charge, although it seemed pretty likely that 2025 MAC Player of the Year Carson Tyler would have at least a decently sized role. Along the way, Kiera Schmidt went from the most reliable returning player on the roster to appearing in just 19 of 26 matches and just 49 of 97 sets. Emma Parks was the only returning outside hitting option of note, and she only logged 70 sets in 23 matches, ultimately only starting twice for the Golden Eagles, which is actually less than Schmidt started. Even the most likely answers to the questions in front of Mendoza ended up being anything but reliable as the season went along. And yet. On Saturday, Emma Parks was the one dropping the kills for the last three points of Marquette’s 3-0 (25-15, 25-22, 25-23) sweep of St. John’s that moved the Golden Eagles to 14-2 in Big East play. With the win, Marquette has clinched at least a share of the 2026 Big East regular season title, which is the fifth Big East title in program history. top.description: Nov 14, 2026; East Lansing, Michigan, USA; Washington Huskies quarterback Demond Williams Jr. (1) hands off the ball to Washington Huskies running back Jayden Limar (17) during the first quarter against the Michigan State Spartans at … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor Big Plays Early and Late Fuel Husky Win at Michigan State. Washington’s eight-play, 78-yard touchdown drive broke a 14-14 tie late in the fourth quarter at Michigan State. Running back Jayden Limar scored what was ultimately the game-winning touchdown to cap a possession that was fueled by explosive plays. Entering that drive, Washington had just one play of 10-plus yards in the second half. All four of its previous second-half possessions ended with a punt and combined for just 41 total yards. The game-winning touchdown drive featured four plays of 10-plus and gave Washington a 21-14 win at Michigan State. Big Plays Fuel Husky Win at Michigan State Explosive Passing Early Demond Williams started the game four for four passing with each throw traveling less than 10 air yards. His next two attempts then traveled 40-plus air yards each but were both overthrown, despite the receivers gaining a step on the defenders. That didn’t prevent Williams from continuing to attack the deep part of the field. Two plays after his deep incompletions, Williams connected with Chris Lawson for a 58-yard touchdown, hitting his receiver in stride as he was tackled across the goal line. It was Lawson’s first reception of 50-plus on the year, and it tied the football game at seven. On the Huskies’ next offensive possession, explosive plays again fueled the drive. Consecutive false start penalties turned a second and one into a second and 11, and Williams immediately responded to the adversity with three-straight explosive throws. He connected with Rashid Williams on a 26-yard sideline pass on the next play. The Husky receiver displayed excellent sideline awareness as he toe-tapped the green grass for a big-play first down. Williams targeted Decker DeGraaf for 33 yards on the next snap, before finding Lawson for a 17-yard touchdown, his second of the game. Lawson finished with 125 receiving yards on five catches (24.8 yards per reception) in what was his third 100-yard game in the last four outings. top.title: Kentucky falls to Florida: 3 things to know and postgame banter
top.description: The Kentucky Wildcats fell to the Florida Gators in Lexington on Saturday night by a final score of 21-14. The Cats came out ready to roll. They forced a Gator punt and then drove down the field on a 15-play, 86-yard drive for the game’s first score. Unfortunately, things slowed down tremendously after that. To make matters worse, the offense didn’t make the defense’s job any easier. After an egregious holding call in the end zone, Florida added two points on a safety, leading to a 7-2 UK lead at halftime. After the break, Kentucky did not come out as ready as you would expect. Kenny Minchey was sacked and fumbled the ball back to Florida on the opening drive of the second half. Florida was able to punch it in, but they decided to try an onside kick on the ensuing kickoff, which flipped all momentum back to the Cats after they recovered it. Kentucky answered with a score of its own to retake the lead 14-10. Once again, however, the Gators were able to consistently move the ball when Kentucky was not able to do the same. A field goal cut the lead to 14-13, and another touchdown extended the Gator lead to seven. Kentucky’s offense couldn’t answer, getting turned over on downs in back-to-back drives, and that was that. A special season has been flipped on its head. Two really disappointing games following an incredible run to start the season. That’s why we play the games. Florida isn’t a good football team, but Jon Sumrall showed why the Gators picked him in this one. Next up, the Cats will travel to CoMo to take on the Missouri Tigers next Saturday night. Two more games to finish out the season, albeit with less to play for coming into this game. The offense has been abysmal Will Stein is widely known as an impressive play-caller, but whether it’s him or Joe Sloan (more likely), the offense has been pretty disappointing for a while now. After scoring just six points on two field goals last week in an embarrassing performance against the Tennessee Volunteers, the Cats struggled for the majority of the night in this one. The offense is somewhat gimmicky. It’s been lacking explosiveness, and when the run game is nonexistent, like it was in this game, Kentucky struggles to get consistent results. top.description: Cypress Ranch will take on Allen at the UIL state championships. (Raquel Natalicchio/Houston Chronicle) Facing a two-set deficit Saturday evening at Delmar Fieldhouse, the Cypress Ranch volleyball team rallied to beat Austin Lake Travis 21-25, 22-25, 25-18, 25-21, 15-9 and secure the program's first state championship appearance. The Mustangs (40-7), who have won 29 consecutive matches, will face Allen (42-2) for the UIL Class 6A Division I title at 6 p.m. next Saturday at the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland. Lake Travis swept Cy Ranch in their first meeting at the Leander Volleypolooza tournament in August, and it looked like the rematch might be headed in the same direction. But the Mustangs, led by coach Collea McKinney, were able to swing the momentum back in their favor and win three consecutive sets to clinch their spot in the final. Regional champions for a second consecutive season, Cy Ranch will face an Allen team that is riding a 20-match winning streak of its own. The Eagles will be making their first state championship appearance since 2003 after sweeping Duncanville in the other semifinal match Saturday at the Thomas Coliseum in Haltom City. Cy Ranch is one of two Houston-area teams headed to state. The other is Lake Creek, which earned its spot in the Class 5A Division II final with a 25-20, 25-14, 25-20 win over New Braunfels at the Merrell Center in Katy. The Lions (43-10) have won 10 consecutive matches and will also be making their first championship match appearance. Lake Creek reached the semifinals in 2022 before losing to eventual champion Colleyville Heritage. Lake Creek, led by coach Kayli Kane, has swept four of its five playoff opponents and will play Abilene Wylie (39-4) for the state title at 11 a.m. next Saturday in Garland. Wylie swept Colleyville Heritage in the other semifinal matchup. The Bulldogs won the Class 3A state title in 2013 and are making their first championship appearance as a 5A program. top.title: Detroit Lions Reveal Uniform Combo for Germany Game
top.description: The Detroit Lions are ready to bring some Honolulu Blue to Germany, and now we know exactly what they’ll be wearing when they take the field against the New England Patriots. Ahead of Sunday’s Week 10 matchup in Munich, the Lions revealed their uniform combination, opting for their traditional Honolulu Blue jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets . The look was featured in a team graphic highlighting wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose German heritage has made this international matchup particularly meaningful. The uniform combination also includes Honolulu Blue socks, giving Detroit a familiar look for its first international regular-season game since 2015. According to NBC Sports’ Week 10 uniform breakdown , the Patriots will counter with silver helmets, white jerseys, and silver pants. Detroit Lions Ready to Represent in Germany The Lions enter Sunday’s game with a 6-2 record and a four-game winning streak following their 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins. New England comes into the matchup at 5-4 after suffering a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Detroit will serve as the designated home team at Munich’s Allianz Arena, and head coach Dan Campbell has already made it clear that he expects plenty of support. Campbell recently declared the Lions “Germany’s team” , pointing to the growing international fan base and St. Brown’s connection to the country. Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp also predicted a blue wave of Detroit supporters in Munich, even taking a playful shot at the lack of Patriots fans she had encountered during the festivities. According to the Lions’ official game-day information , Sunday’s matchup will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX , which is 3:30 p.m. local time in Germany. Detroit will be looking for its fifth consecutive victory while giving its international supporters something to celebrate. nigeria.title: Sex agreement should be part of marriage contract
nigeria.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. It is practical, it is respectful, and it is necessary for a healthy modern marriage. nigeria.description: By Dayo Oyinlola Institutions are ecosystems made up of individual units that live in symbiotic relationships with each other. In these environments, information is processed dynamically and learning occurs both formally and informally. We must consider this reality when discussing leadership development. Leaders learn through written documents and institutional codes of conduct: values, laws, behavioral manuals, KPIs and OKRs that organisations establish to hold leaders accountable. And then there are the experiences nobody formally teaches, but everyone learns. A young executive watches how decisions are made. They notice who gets rewarded and who gets overlooked. They observe what happens when someone challenges authority, misses a target, refuses to compromise or asks an uncomfortable question. Nobody necessarily sits them down to teach these lessons. We often think of leadership development as something that happens through formal training, coaching, mentoring and experience. All of these matters, but leaders are also continuously shaped by the systems, institutions, cultures and circumstances within which they operate. And sometimes, the lessons being taught by the environment are very different from the lesson’s organisations believe they are teaching. Consider an organisation that claims to encourage employees to challenge ideas, yet senior leaders consistently dismiss people who disagree with them. Employees then learn that deference is safer than speaking up. Over time, people respond to what they experience rather than what they are told. The environment teaches what is rewarded. It teaches what is tolerated. It teaches how power works, whose voice matters and whether speaking up is valued or punished. It teaches people what leadership really means when it is exercised, not what the organisation says leadership means. This becomes particularly important in difficult operating environments. But there is another question worth asking: What happens when the environment consistently makes the wrong behaviour easier than the right one? If people repeatedly experience an environment where ethical behaviour is punished and unethical behaviour is rewarded, the environment itself becomes part of their leadership development. This is why integrity cannot survive indefinitely as an individual act of courage. For it to become sustainable, it must become part of the collective environment. nigeria.title: It’s time for results, by Funmi Komolafe
nigeria.description: Beloved, it is mid November already. Some are counting the number of days left for 2026 to roll away; others are counting down towards political events in their country. As a Christian what is the focus of your count down? Yours should be a count down to the physical manifestation of your miracle; it should be a count down to the expiration of a challenge in your life. In other words, the count down to the end of 2026 should be for a Christian the time to celebrate results. The one that would celebrate would not give up. However, as human being, we tend to feel disappointed when we have not been able to attain the goals that we set for ourselves. Beloved, lamentations, wearing mournful looks, depression, suicide attempts, all of these do not produce positive results. These expressions should not be associated with a Christian that has deep faith in God and the ability of God to meet all needs. Philippians 2 vs. 13-16 ( KJV) tells us : “ For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. nigeria.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. nigeria.title: Nigeria needs 700,000 housing units annually to tackle deficit, Durojaye says
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Chairman of the Board of Directors of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, Samuel Durojaye, has said that Nigeria needs to construct approximately 700,000 housing units annually over the next decade to significantly reduce its housing deficit. Durojaye noted that achieving the target would require sustained investment, improved access to housing finance and greater collaboration among key stakeholders in the real estate and mortgage sectors. Durojaye, who disclosed this at the 9th Annual General Meeting of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, held in Abeokuta, Ogun State described mortgage institutions as vital to bridging the country’s housing gap, explaining that they play a dual role in facilitating homeownership for individuals and providing property developers with access to the financing needed to expand housing construction. He stressed that strengthening mortgage financing would improve the capacity of developers to deliver more housing units and make homeownership more accessible to Nigerians. He added that increasing the supply of affordable housing would help ease pressure on the property market, particularly by moderating the persistent rise in rental costs across major urban centres. According to him, addressing the housing deficit requires a sustained focus on expanding housing supply and improving access to affordable financing to ensure that more Nigerians can secure decent and affordable homes. The chairman, however, identified access to long-term funding as one of the major constraints confronting mortgage banks, explaining that the long repayment periods associated with housing loans made it difficult for institutions to rely on short-term deposits. “The minimum tenure for a mortgage is 10, 15 or 20 years. You cannot take people’s money when they expect it back in 90 days and put it into a property that will not pay back until 15 years,” he said. He therefore called for funding arrangements that would align with the long-term nature of mortgage financing, stressing that sustainable access to capital was essential for expanding homeownership. Durojaye also urged Nigerians, particularly young professionals and salary earners, to embrace mortgage financing early in their careers, rather than commit substantial portions of their income to recurring rent payments. “Instead of paying ₦2m in rent every year, why don’t you buy a house and start paying ₦200,000 monthly from your salary?” he asked. He explained that mortgage arrangements enabled prospective homeowners to spread the cost of acquiring properties over an agreed period, allowing them to build long-term assets instead of continually spending on rent. nigeria.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
nigeria.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. nigeria.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
nigeria.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. sports.description: The Detroit Pistons have received some concerning injury news during Saturday night’s matchup against the Miami Heat, and it involves one of their most productive offensive players. Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press initially noted Robinson’s absence after halftime, reporting that the veteran sharpshooter had not returned to the floor. sports.description: Fiji boss Jake White (left) believes Andy Farrell (right) and Ireland must improve before facing South Africa [Getty Images] Former South Africa head coach Jake White said his Fiji side "did Ireland a favour" in Saturday's Nations Championship contest before the Irish face the Springboks in Dublin next week. Fiji lost 43-15 to Ireland at Aviva Stadium having frustrated Andy Farrell's side during a closely contested first half. While Ireland scored 26 unanswered points in the second half, White - who led South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007 - said Andy Farrell's team cannot afford similarly sluggish spells against the back-to-back world champions. "We were playing a little bit like South Africa to be honest, I think that sums it up," said the 62-year-old. "We were letting Ireland have the ball and we were happy to defend against them and we were happy for them to try to outwork us." Asked to assess Ireland and South Africa's highly-anticipated meeting on Saturday (16:40 GMT), White added: "Well, I think we probably did Ireland a favour today. "Let me put it that way, because I think Ireland deep down know that if they play like that against South Africa, they're gonna be up against it." Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji White, who was appointed Fiji boss last month, was frustrated that his side opted to take a tap penalty instead of a scrum when the game was in the balance in the second half. "I know how South Africa operate and they would've taken that scrum there, they would have backed the fact that they wanted to get [Ireland] a yellow card," said White. "They would have taken another scrum and another scrum and another scrum, and they wouldn't have worried about the ref making a call about collapsing or early engaging. "The five-metre line-outs that we didn't take opportunities in, and the five-metre scrum and tap penalties, South Africa will turn those into points and I'm sure that Andy [Farrell] and the players will be aware of that. "They [Ireland] have been around a long time, and they know what's coming, and that's probably why he picked the team that he did because he wanted to make sure that they get a little bit more gun-ready for next weekend, because the easiest thing would have been to change the team and then they're probably one game shy of playing South Africa next week." sports.title: Kentucky falls to Florida: 3 things to know and postgame banter
sports.description: The Kentucky Wildcats fell to the Florida Gators in Lexington on Saturday night by a final score of 21-14. The Cats came out ready to roll. They forced a Gator punt and then drove down the field on a 15-play, 86-yard drive for the game’s first score. Unfortunately, things slowed down tremendously after that. To make matters worse, the offense didn’t make the defense’s job any easier. After an egregious holding call in the end zone, Florida added two points on a safety, leading to a 7-2 UK lead at halftime. After the break, Kentucky did not come out as ready as you would expect. Kenny Minchey was sacked and fumbled the ball back to Florida on the opening drive of the second half. Florida was able to punch it in, but they decided to try an onside kick on the ensuing kickoff, which flipped all momentum back to the Cats after they recovered it. Kentucky answered with a score of its own to retake the lead 14-10. Once again, however, the Gators were able to consistently move the ball when Kentucky was not able to do the same. sports.description: Cypress Ranch will take on Allen at the UIL state championships. (Raquel Natalicchio/Houston Chronicle) Facing a two-set deficit Saturday evening at Delmar Fieldhouse, the Cypress Ranch volleyball team rallied to beat Austin Lake Travis 21-25, 22-25, 25-18, 25-21, 15-9 and secure the program's first state championship appearance. The Mustangs (40-7), who have won 29 consecutive matches, will face Allen (42-2) for the UIL Class 6A Division I title at 6 p.m. next Saturday at the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland. Lake Travis swept Cy Ranch in their first meeting at the Leander Volleypolooza tournament in August, and it looked like the rematch might be headed in the same direction. But the Mustangs, led by coach Collea McKinney, were able to swing the momentum back in their favor and win three consecutive sets to clinch their spot in the final. Regional champions for a second consecutive season, Cy Ranch will face an Allen team that is riding a 20-match winning streak of its own. The Eagles will be making their first state championship appearance since 2003 after sweeping Duncanville in the other semifinal match Saturday at the Thomas Coliseum in Haltom City. Cy Ranch is one of two Houston-area teams headed to state. The other is Lake Creek, which earned its spot in the Class 5A Division II final with a 25-20, 25-14, 25-20 win over New Braunfels at the Merrell Center in Katy. The Lions (43-10) have won 10 consecutive matches and will also be making their first championship match appearance. Lake Creek reached the semifinals in 2022 before losing to eventual champion Colleyville Heritage. Lake Creek, led by coach Kayli Kane, has swept four of its five playoff opponents and will play Abilene Wylie (39-4) for the state title at 11 a.m. next Saturday in Garland. Wylie swept Colleyville Heritage in the other semifinal matchup. The Bulldogs won the Class 3A state title in 2013 and are making their first championship appearance as a 5A program. sports.title: Detroit Lions Reveal Uniform Combo for Germany Game
sports.description: The Detroit Lions are ready to bring some Honolulu Blue to Germany, and now we know exactly what they’ll be wearing when they take the field against the New England Patriots. Ahead of Sunday’s Week 10 matchup in Munich, the Lions revealed their uniform combination, opting for their traditional Honolulu Blue jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets . The look was featured in a team graphic highlighting wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, whose German heritage has made this international matchup particularly meaningful. According to NBC Sports’ Week 10 uniform breakdown , the Patriots will counter with silver helmets, white jerseys, and silver pants. New England comes into the matchup at 5-4 after suffering a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Detroit will serve as the designated home team at Munich’s Allianz Arena, and head coach Dan Campbell has already made it clear that he expects plenty of support. Campbell recently declared the Lions “Germany’s team” , pointing to the growing international fan base and St. Brown’s connection to the country. Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp also predicted a blue wave of Detroit supporters in Munich, even taking a playful shot at the lack of Patriots fans she had encountered during the festivities. According to the Lions’ official game-day information , Sunday’s matchup will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX , which is 3:30 p.m. local time in Germany. sports.description: The Rich Rebels celebrate with their trophy after winning against the Milford Tigers during a 1A 8-player state championship held at Eccles Coliseum in Cedar City on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News Rich’s dynasty in 8-player football doesn’t show any signs of slowing down. In a rematch of last year’s title game, top-seed Rich rolled past No. 2 seed Milford 69-35 at Southern Utah University on Saturday evening to claim its fourth straight 1A 8-player state championship. “It’s really surreal. It’s an awesome experience. Words can’t describe it,” said Rich senior Wilkes Weston, who had a monster performance Saturday with 194 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Rich beat Milford 65-19 in Week 2 this season, breaking the game open in the second half after leading by just seven at intermission. Three months later, Rich didn’t wait around in blowing the game open. Its offense scored every time it touched the ball but once the entire game, building a 35-14 halftime lead and coasting from there. “We believed we had an edge in this game, and I was grateful that the kids came and tried to take it rather than just be entitled to winning,” said Rich coach Tyson Larsen. “I felt like they came out and tried to take the victory and leave no doubt rather than just assume that because we beat them earlier in the year that it would happen again.” Weston set the tone on the first drive of the game, scoring on a 2-yard run, and after Milford tied the game 8-8 on the ensuing possession, Weston scored again on Rich’s second possession to stretch the lead to 14-8. Weston had high praise for his linemen after the game. “Those holes were massive for me to run through, so I could just keep on running all day long through those things,” Weston said. While Weston had a workhorse performance with 31 carries, fellow running backs Brady Cornia and Jasper Johnson benefited from those gaping holes with explosive plays. Cornia carried the ball five times for 124 yards and two touchdowns — including a 90-yard TD run — while Johnson ripped off two touchdowns and 90 rushing yards on just two carries. Already firmly in control at halftime, Cornia’s 90-yard run was the exclamation point for the Rebels. Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms. Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket. Read full article Comments

science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972.
